prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from airport bag-drop acceptance or transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up, and aircraft-loading handoff. System boundary includes airport equipment and control functions that convey, screen, route, reconcile, and stage baggage; excludes airline aircraft loading beyond handoff at the outbound load control point.
Elements and responsibilities:
• Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit captures bag identification at the passenger interface and accepts baggage for processing.
• Transfer Bag Feeder separately inducts eligible transfer baggage.
• Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags in a controlled manner to screening and sorting equipment.
• Baggage Control System (alias Velvet) coordinates bag status, routing decisions, and operational visibility across connected equipment; uses current flight and operating data to support routing and alignment with scheduled departures.
• Concourse Zone Controller (alias Mosslight) coordinates local equipment and conveyance within its assigned operating area; produces Recovery Route Card.
• Flight Data Gateway sends Flight Cutoff Advisory; recipient unspecified.
• Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes cleared bags toward applicable make-up areas.
• North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner provide baggage screening interfaces.
• Image Resolution Desk supports operator review of screening images when automated processing requires assessment.
• Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled path for bags selected for additional examination.
• Explosives Response Team and Security Duty Manager coordinate security response and disposition for escalated screening events.
• Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification of bag identity and processing status when records or physical handling require reconciliation.
• East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor convey routed baggage toward relevant loading areas.
• Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit stages baggage for its assigned departure operation.
• Outbound Load Control Desk provides the interface for confirming baggage readiness at aircraft-loading handoff.
• Airline Ramp Coordinator coordinates acceptance of staged baggage for ramp operations.
No explicit modes or normative requirements stated.

New part:
S024: The Baggage Operations Supervisor oversees routine flow, responds to service interruptions, and coordinates operational recovery with the Security Duty Manager and Maintenance Technician.
S025: Service objectives are to maintain safe screening, accurate bag-to-flight association, predictable throughput, and timely delivery within applicable departure cutoffs.
S026: Equipment status, bag identity, routing state, and operating restrictions are exchanged through defined interfaces, with local staff responsible for resolving conditions that automated controls cannot clear.
S027: Check-in acceptance begins when staff confirm that the bag is eligible for carriage under the applicable airline rules.
S028: Staff verify the passenger and flight details before accepting the bag into the checked-baggage process.
S029: The Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records the accepted bag and initiates its processing.
S030: The Bag Tag Printer produces a durable tag with a unique identifier for each accepted bag.
S031: The tag identifier is associated with the passenger and flight record in the Baggage Control System.
S032: The Baggage Control System checks that the flight is open for bag acceptance and that the bag record is complete.
S033: Bags with missing, unreadable, or conflicting acceptance data are held for staff resolution before induction.
S034: Staff check bag dimensions and weight against the configured limits for standard conveyor handling.
S035: The Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit sends an Oversize Exception Ticket when a checked bag exceeds the configured size envelope.
S036: Oversized bags remain in a designated holding area until staff confirm an approved handling route.
S037: The Transfer Bag Feeder identifies each inbound transfer bag and records its arrival into the local handling process.
S038: The Transfer Bag Feeder sends a Late Transfer Bag Card when a bag enters from an inbound transfer stream.
S039: Staff confirm that transfer-bag identifiers are legible and correspond to a valid onward flight record.
S040: The Baggage Control System compares transfer-bag data with the current routing information before the bag is released for induction.
S041: The Flight Data Gateway supplies flight and routing records used for acceptance and induction decisions.
S042: Before induction, the bag record must be valid, the selected route must be available, and the receiving equipment must be ready.
S043: The Concourse Zone Controller grants an induction permissive only when local equipment status and operating restrictions allow movement.
S044: The Induction Tray Conveyor accepts bags through controlled feed points and maintains separation between successive bags.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
